h1: The 5 Best 18V Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five cordless leaf blowers on the Milwaukee M18 18V platform, including brand-name tools and battery-compatible budget options.
summary: The Milwaukee M18 FUEL at 450 CFM and 120 MPH is the best 18V leaf blower here, thanks to a brushless motor and clear specs. Compatible blowers from ALDIPRO and Houselife list more CFM for less money. The compact 0884-20 is for light patio work, and the second FUEL listing is for buyers willing to research.
intro: Nobody buys an 18 volt blower for the blower. The tool is the cheap part, and the battery is the lasting purchase. Pick the wrong platform and you inherit a second charger, a second set of packs and a shelf of cells that fit nothing else you own. That is why the first question here is not airflow but whose battery you already have.

Every pick in this ranking runs on Milwaukee's M18 platform, either as a Milwaukee tool or as a blower that states M18 compatibility. We reviewed five on listed airflow, motor type, battery inclusion and price bucket, and dropped blowers built for other battery systems. Check whether the battery ships in the box, because several listings here sell the tool alone.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL 120 MPH 450 CFM 18-Volt Lithium Ion Brushless
products.verdict: A brushless 18V handheld with 120 MPH and 450 CFM.
products.description:
The M18 FUEL is a handheld brushless blower listed at 120 MPH and 450 CFM, in the $100 to $200 bucket. Brushless matters on a battery tool: with no carbon brushes to wear, the motor wastes less energy as heat, which stretches a charge and extends the life of the motor. The two figures describe different jobs. Speed lifts wet or stuck debris, while volume pushes whole piles.

It wins by pairing a brand's brushless line with two stated airflow numbers. The compatible blowers below list more CFM, but none is a Milwaukee tool or lists both figures.

Buy it if you already own M18 batteries. The caveat is value: ALDIPRO and Houselife list 700 and 600 CFM for a lower bucket. Check whether a battery comes in the box.
products.idealFor: M18 owners wanting a brand-name blower.
products.skipIf: You want the most CFM per dollar.

products.name: Milwaukee Electric - M18 FUELTRADE Blower
products.verdict: A second FUEL-line blower with few listed specs.
products.description:
This second Milwaukee blower sits on the M18 platform in the $100 to $200 bucket, and the listing shows no airflow or speed figure. You are left with the brand and the FUEL name, and a spec sheet that cannot be compared with anything else in the ranking.

It takes second place on the strength of that brand, not on measurable performance. Milwaukee's FUEL line usually signals a brushless motor and a more robust build, but the listing does not confirm it for this model. Compared with the top FUEL blower, which states 450 CFM and 120 MPH, this one asks for faith.

Buy it if you are an M18 loyalist and will research the full listing for airflow, weight and battery inclusion. Skip it if you want numbers up front, since the first pick gives you those and costs the same bucket.
products.idealFor: M18 loyalists who will research specs.

products.name: Milwaukee 0884-20 M18 18 Volt Cordless Compact Yard Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A compact handheld yard blower at 100 CFM and 160 MPH.
products.description:
The Milwaukee 0884-20 is a compact handheld yard blower, listed at 100 CFM and 160 MPH, in the $100 to $200 bucket. That combination tells you how it behaves. High speed from a narrow nozzle lifts light debris off a hard surface, but 100 CFM is a small volume, so it clears a path rather than a lawn.

It ranks third because 100 CFM is far lower than the others, even though the 160 MPH number looks impressive. Speed without volume moves leaves in a thin stripe. The M18 FUEL at 450 CFM covers four and a half times the volume.

Buy it for patios, steps and sweeping grass clippings off a driveway. It is a tool-only model, so you need an M18 battery. Skip it if you clear piles of fall leaves, where the volume gap shows quickly.

products.name: ALDIPRO 700 CFM Leaf Blower Compatible with Milwaukee M18 Battery
products.verdict: 700 CFM on an M18 battery, at the lowest price bucket.
products.description:
The ALDIPRO is a cordless blower listed at 700 CFM and compatible with Milwaukee M18 batteries, in the $50 to $100 bucket. It lists the most airflow in this ranking, 250 CFM above the M18 FUEL, and it is cheaper.

It ranks fourth for the reasons that never show in a spec table. It is not a Milwaukee tool and has no brand support behind it, so a failed switch or a cracked housing is a seller problem. The listing does not state a motor type, and a listed CFM from a lesser-known maker is a claim rather than a verified figure. Battery is not included either.

Buy it if you hold spare M18 packs and want maximum airflow for little money. Skip it if you do not own M18 batteries, since the pack costs more than the blower.
products.skipIf: You do not own M18 packs.

products.name: Houselife 600 CFM Cordless Leaf Blower Compatible with Milwaukee 18V M18 Battery
products.verdict: A 600 CFM handheld that takes M18 batteries.
products.description:
The Houselife is a handheld cordless blower listed at 600 CFM and compatible with Milwaukee 18V M18 batteries, in the $50 to $100 bucket. It gives you a large airflow figure at a modest price, and it is built for owners who want to avoid buying a branded blower.

It finishes behind the ALDIPRO because it lists 100 CFM less in the same bucket. Against the Milwaukee M18 FUEL, it lists 150 CFM more for a lower price, but without the brushless motor or the brand's support.

Buy it for low-cost yard work if you already own M18 batteries. Battery is not included, and the listing shows no motor type. Skip it if you want a Milwaukee tool with warranty support, or if you want the extra 100 CFM the ALDIPRO lists.

whatMatters.detail: A blower that uses batteries you already own saves the cost of a second pack and charger, which can cost as much as the tool itself. This matters more than the blower itself. Check the compatibility statement in the title, such as M18 or 18V, and confirm it matches your battery brand exactly, not just the voltage.

Tool-only listings sell the blower without a battery or charger, while kits include them. The price gap between the two can be large. Read the listing before you assume the battery is in the box, and check the questions section if the title is ambiguous, because sellers often reuse photos that show a battery.

CFM is air volume and MPH is air speed. Volume moves piles of leaves, while speed lifts stuck debris from cracks. A strong blower lists both, and a listing that shows only one is hiding the other, as with the 0884-20's low CFM. Look for both numbers and compare like for like.

A brushless motor has no carbon brushes to wear out, so it runs more efficiently and lasts longer, which stretches battery life. It matters most on cordless tools where runtime is limited. Look for the word brushless in the title, as on the M18 FUEL, and be cautious when a compatible blower is silent on it, since it may well be a brushed motor.

Compatible blowers cost less and often list more CFM, but lack the brand's support and parts network. A branded tool brings warranty service and a track record. Decide if you value the name, and check seller details, return terms and who handles a warranty claim before ordering a compatible model.

faq.q: Do these blowers include a battery?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Check each listing carefully, since several are tool-only and the photos can mislead. The ALDIPRO and Houselife both state that the battery is not included, and the 0884-20 also needs an M18 pack.
Buying a blower for a different battery system than the one you own. The tool is the cheap part, but a second platform means a second charger and packs. Confirm M18 or 18V compatibility in the title.

faq.q: Is the Milwaukee worth it over the ALDIPRO?
faq.a: If you value the brand and the brushless motor, yes. The ALDIPRO lists 700 CFM against the Milwaukee's 450 for a lower bucket, but it offers no brand support or stated motor type.

Read the title and confirm M18 or 18V is stated. The ALDIPRO and Houselife both name Milwaukee M18 compatibility, and the Milwaukee blowers are native. Check the product questions if the title is unclear, and look at the battery interface photos.

faq.q: How do I care for the battery?
faq.a: Store it per the maker's manual and charge it with the correct charger. Keep the pack out of extreme heat and cold, and avoid leaving it fully drained for long periods between seasons, since a deeply discharged pack can lose capacity.

faq.q: Why does the 0884-20 list low CFM?
faq.a: It is a compact model built for light work, at 100 CFM and 160 MPH. The high speed lifts light debris, but the low volume means it suits patios and paths, not leaf piles, and it takes many passes on heavy cover.

finalTake: Buy the Milwaukee M18 FUEL if you already own M18 batteries and want a brand-name brushless blower. Take the ALDIPRO or Houselife when airflow per dollar matters and you have spare packs. Keep the 0884-20 for patios and paths. Confirm the battery is included before you order any of them.
